After 13 years of trading, four blown accounts, and more mistakes than I can count, I’ve learned something most traders spend years avoiding.

The market isn’t nearly as complicated as we make it.

We overcomplicate things.

More indicators. More strategies. More information. More opinions.

It won’t.

You can know exactly where a stock is going and still lose money.

You can have the perfect setup and still execute poorly.

You can make money on a terrible trade and lose money on a great one.

Here’s what I’ve learned:

You don’t need more setups.

Doing nothing is a skill.

Confidence comes from keeping promises to yourself.

A good trade can lose money. A bad trade can make money.

Missing a move costs you nothing.

Your biggest advantage is controlling yourself.

Trading will expose your impatience, greed, ego, and fear faster than almost anything else out there.

I’ve spent over a decade studying charts.

The hardest part has always been learning to manage myself.

And maybe that’s the lesson.

You can spend your entire life trying to understand the market, only to realize that you just needed to understand yourself.
